indicators.description: UAVs on a cell another UAV occupies, this step, base cells excluded

indicators.creator: rismail

indicators.description: Pairs within 6 cells, this step, base excluded, full-separation mode

indicators.description: Lowest tank fraction among UAVs not on the base

indicators.description: Share of the grid viewed in the last 56 steps (one lap), defined from step 56

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: OK

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: While fighting, UAVs never share a cell: every flight, whether scouting, fighting, refuelling or refilling, stops short of any UAV in view and of any cell a teammate was sent through. Source: POL-SFF-7, POL-FF-11, 12, 13.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Unless a UAV is told it is somewhere it is not, in which case it can leave its flying zone. Measured (100 runs, final settings, position error on): 1.89 collisions per run (max 6), 0.38 UAVs lost per run, coverage 62.7%

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Seven tests show every flight stops short of visible UAVs and is no longer than the UAV can see, and that the base is shared airspace (POL-SCT-6, 7, 8).

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: OK

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Five tests show a blocked UAV off its loop steps aside, including a head-on meeting in the base row (POL-SCT-13).

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: In 100 runs of the final configuration every fire still burning 20 steps after ignition was detected (97 of 97), on average 11.7 steps after ignition.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: OK

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Each UAV is given a lane of its own, and no two lanes share a column.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: OK

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: One lap covers the whole lane, and a lane that cannot hold a loop is held. Source: POL-SCT-5, 9.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: In 100 runs of the final configuration the sweep covered 97.7% of the grid, and every fire still burning 20 steps after ignition was detected (97 of 97), on average 11.7 steps after ignition.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: OK

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: But only one team size (8 UAVs) was tested, so the number of firefighters is shown to be sufficient, not appropriate, and nothing here varies how far the fire starts from the base. Addressed by: nothing yet.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Requirement specification. POL-SCT-2: a UAV sweeping its lane stays in its flying zone, and no two loops come closer than the separation.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Losses due to mid-air collisions are mitigated.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: OK

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: But separation is not guaranteed in transit: a UAV leaving the base or going to refuel is off its loop. Addressed by: the trimming (C0009) only. Measured: in 1,000 final runs UAVs came closer than 6 cells in every run (89.7 pair-steps per run on average, at most 117), with no collision.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: The lowest end-of-run tank of any UAV in 1,000 runs of the scout policy was 234 of 800.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: OK

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: A UAV without water goes home and waits to be refilled, and the fuel test outranks fighting. Source: POL-SFF-4, 5.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: OK

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: But zero collisions only bounds the rate: with 1,000 runs the 95% upper bound is about 0.3% of runs (3 / 1,000). Not a guarantee. Addressed by: a larger batch, not yet run.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Firefighting UAVs will extinguish fire near the base.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: But scouting is not shown to cause the gain. In 1,000 runs at the final settings, 8 firefighters with no scouts kept the base in 919 (91.9%) against 711 (71.1%) for the scout-firefighter policy, so adding scouts lowered survival by 20.8 points (95% interval 17.5 to 24.1). Addressed by: nothing. The firefighter-only arm is in the results PDF.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Performance. The UAV fleet provides sufficient protection for the home base.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: But the firefighters do not keep the 6-cell separation: in firefighter-only runs UAVs were within 6 cells of each other on 1,741.9 of a possible 1,792 pair-steps per run, and on 281.6 per run (at most 1,183) with scouts and firefighters. Only shared cells are prevented. Addressed by: nothing; there were 0 collisions in 1,000 runs of each.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Unless a UAV has strayed far enough that the flat fuel reserve is too small to get it home. Addressed by: measurement. In 1,000 runs of the scout-firefighter policy and 1,000 of firefighter-only, no UAV ran out of fuel.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Scout UAVs will detect fire near the home base.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Tests show no two UAVs on their loops come closer than SECURITY_DISTANCE, including when the team is out of step (POL-SCT-2). At the final settings the closest approach on the loops was 7.0 cells (100 runs).

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: But the loop keeps no memory, so a lap finishes only if one tank is enough. Addressed by: measurement. With smoke off, coverage at 64 steps is 97.7% (100 runs).

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Res

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Two tests (POL-SFF-6) and three tests (POL-FF-10) show no two UAVs are given the same fire. Tests (POL-FF-7, 8; POL-SFF-3) show the nearest free fire is chosen, and a fire beside an out building outranks a nearer one.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Unless smoke hides UAVs from the trimming, or position error corrupts the positions it uses. Addressed by: nothing in the policy.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Coverage at 64 steps with smoke off is 97.7% (100 runs).

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Losses due to depleted fuel are mitigated: fuel outranks the sweep, and a UAV on the base waits for a full tank. Source: POL-SCT-10, 11, 12

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Res

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: One lap of the sweep loop brings every cell of every lane into view. Source: POL-SCT-3, 4, 5, 9.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: A UAV that has nothing to fight carries on scouting. Source: POL-SFF-1, 2, 8.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: The number of scout and firefighting UAVs is appropriate.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: OK

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Tests show a UAV anywhere on the grid reaches its loop and follows it all the way round (POL-SCT-3, 4).

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Tests show lanes never share a column and run left to right by UAV id (POL-SCT-1).

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: But when a UAV is lost, the survivors’ lanes widen and shift. Addressed by: the lane-shift tests (below). Not exercised in a simulation run: no UAV was lost in 1,000 runs. The tests do not cover trimming during the cross-over

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: With firefighting added (scout-firefighter), the base survived 711 of 1,000 runs, against 473 with scouts only and 487 with no UAVs. The gain over scouts only is 23.8 points (95% interval 19.6 to 28.0, p < 0.001).

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: A blocked UAV that is off its loop steps aside instead of waiting for ever.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: A UAV off its loop reaches it, and a UAV on it follows it all the way round. Source: POL-SCT-3, 4.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Six tests (POL-SFF-3) show a sighting hands a UAV to firefighting: it dumps water when the fire is in drop range and flies toward it otherwise. Three tests (POL-FF-5, 6) show the same rules in the firefighter policy.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: In 1,000 runs of the final configuration with the scout policy: 0 collisions, 0 UAVs lost, 0 UAVs out of fuel. The lowest end-of-run tank of any UAV in any run was 234 of 800. Source: results/final_2_scout_only.json

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Four tests (POL-SFF-7) and seven tests (POL-FF-11, 12, 13) show flights are trimmed to stop short of other UAVs and are no longer than a UAV can see, and the base is shared airspace.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Unless the policy is called under a managing system, which calls it once per group of UAVs and divides the grid by the group size, so lanes overlap. Addressed by: scope. The claim holds only when the policy is flown alone (X0002).

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: But 1,000 runs with no losses cannot show the fleet would stay in service with positioning error or smoke on. Measured with position error on: 0.38 UAVs lost per run (100 runs). Addressed by: nothing in the policy.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Tests show one lap brings every cell of the lane into view, even for a UAV that joins half-way, and a lane that cannot hold a loop is held (POL-SCT-5, 9).

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Four tests (POL-SFF-1, 2, 8) show a UAV with no fire to fight flies the scout’s action, and a UAV that stops to fight does not move the lanes of the ones still scouting.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Lane-shift tests remove one of 8 UAVs (ids 0, 3 and 7) and fly the survivors on. The survivors’ lanes still tile the grid and are wider than before, and every survivor ends up on a loop of its new lane (POL-SCT-1, 3, 6)

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Res

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Every flight stops short of visible UAVs and of cells a teammate was sent through, is no longer than the UAV can see, and the home base is shared airspace.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Unless smoke hides cells inside a UAV’s window, in which case coverage is lower than measured. Addressed by: nothing. Smoke was off in every run.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: The number of scout UAVs is appropriate to detect nearby fire.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Safety: The risk of losing UAVs while they fly the scout and scout-firefighter policies is acceptably low.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Faux Claim: The scout and scout-firefighter policies keep the UAV team safe and protect the home base, in the configurations where their stated assumptions hold.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Res

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: OK

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: The fleet stays in service: no UAV is lost, stuck or out of fuel, so the sweep continues.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: A UAV that has seen a fire flies to it and drops water once the fire is in range. Source: POL-SFF-3, POL-FF-5, 6.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: OK

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: The probability of collision is low for the chosen separation distance and policy assignment.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: But a lane out of reach of the base makes the UAV turn back before it arrives, and trimmed flights burn idle fuel the estimate does not count. Addressed by: measurement. With the reserve set to 0, flights were identical in all 1,000 runs, because no UAV reached the turn-for-home threshold in a 64-step run (lowest tank 244 of 800). Not shown for longer runs.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: But the win rates depend on the water extinguish probabilities (0.855 at the centre of a drop and 0.54 at the edge), which were chosen to reach a 70/30 target and are not the committed defaults. Addressed by: nothing. The values are stated in X0002.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: OK

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: OK

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Res

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: OK

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: OK

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: But position error causes collisions. Measured with position error on: 1.89 collisions per run (max 6), 0.38 UAVs lost per run. Addressed by: nothing in the policy

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Argue that the current UAV configuration provides sufficient protection.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: The scout never drops water, so scout-only survival (47.3%) is not different from no UAVs (48.7%, p = 0.53). Base protection depends on a firefighting policy. Source: results/final_1_baseline.json, results/final_2_scout_only.json.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Eleven tests show the turn-for-home point, one-step lookahead, payload surcharge, waiting for a full tank, and silence without fuel tracking (POL-SCT-10, 11, 12).

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: With the fuel reserve set to 0 (final settings otherwise), 1,000 runs gave 0 collisions, 0 UAVs lost and 0 UAVs out of fuel, and the same 473 base survivals as with reserve 0.1.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Res

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Final configuration: 100 x 100 grid, 8 UAVs (none in the no-UAV arm), tank 800, fuel reserve 0.1, SECURITY_DISTANCE 6, UAV speed 5, observation radius 4, 64-step runs, flown alone (managing none), positioning error and smoke occlusion off unless stated. Water extinguish probability 0.855 at the centre of a drop and 0.54 at the edge. Each arm is 1,000 runs with seeds 20261018 + N, and the base surviving the run counts as a win.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Res

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: OK

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: OK

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: OK

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: With 8 firefighters and no scouts the base survived 919 of 1,000 runs, against 487 with no UAVs (+43.2 points, 95% interval 39.7 to 46.8, p < 0.001).

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: The scout policy maintains a minimum separation between UAVs sweeping their lanes: never closer than SECURITY_DISTANCE. Source: POL-SCT-2.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: But one lap costs about 466 to 469 fuel from the loop start (56 steps, 9 per full-speed step). With a tank of 800 and a 10% reserve, a UAV whose lane is far from the base cannot fly a lap and the trip out and back in one sortie. Addressed by: measurement. In 64-step runs the lowest end-of-run tank was 234 of 800, so no UAV needs to refuel for a lap. Not shown for longer runs.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: In 1,000 runs of the scout-firefighter policy and 1,000 of the firefighter-only policy: 0 collisions, 0 UAVs lost, 0 UAVs out of fuel. The lowest end-of-run tank of any UAV was 226.8 of 800 (scout-firefighter) and 702.8 of 800 (firefighter only).

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Res

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: But a lap takes about 56 steps and the final runs are 64 steps, with ignition at step 10 to 20. A fire can start behind a UAV and go unseen for most of a lap. Addressed by: measurement. In 100 runs at the final settings every fire still burning 20 steps after ignition was detected (97 of 97), on average 11.7 steps after ignition.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Res

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Res

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Res

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: The number of firefighters is appropriate for the proximity of the fire to the base.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Three tests (POL-SFF-5) show a UAV without water flies home and waits to be refilled. Three tests (POL-SFF-4) show the fuel test outranks fighting.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Argue that the reasons a UAV could be lost are mitigated: an empty tank and a mid-air collision.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: OK

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: OK

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: OK

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: No two UAVs are sent to the same fire, and a fire threatening an out building is attacked first. Source: POL-SFF-3, 6, POL-FF-7, 8, 10.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: Argue the two goals separately. Four nodes (lanes, no deadlock, fuel and the 1,000-run results) are shared by both goals and linked under each, so a defeater on one weakens both.

nodes.creator: rismail
nodes.text: OK
